paper_metadata.title: Development of High-Strength High-Temperature Cast Al-Ni-Cr Alloys Through Evolution of a Novel Composite Eutectic Structure

evidence.quote: this article reports a new class of multiphase Al alloys in the Al-Ni-Cr system
Using binary Al-Al3Ni eutectic (Al-3.1Ni) samples for benchmarking, we have studied three alloys with varying additions of Cr along the line AD (Figure 1).
We shall designate these as Al-4Ni-0.5Cr, Al-4Ni-0.6Cr, and Al-5Ni-0.7Cr.

prepared using constituent elements of 99.99 pct purity through arc meting under an argon atmosphere following evacuation of the melting chamber under a vacuum of 10-5 mbar. The alloys were remelted at least 8 times to ensure homogeneity.
The arc-melted buttons were chill cast using a vacuum suction casting setup equipped with a water-cooled split copper mold to obtain rods of 3-mm diameter and 80-mm length.

evidence.quote: The high magnification image of the eutectic colony, as depicted on the right side of Figure 2(a), shows the dual morphology.

Inter-rod spacing for Al-4Ni-0.6Cr alloy is much smaller than the spacing observed in Al-Al3Ni eutectic (370 ± 58 nm for Al-3.1Ni alloy).

These eutectics show good mechanical properties due to the presence of hard intermetallic phases that impede the dislocation motion and, hence, impart strength.

mechanisms.name: crack bridging
mechanisms.material_state: as-cast, 30 pct deformed in compression at room temperature

evidence.quote: The presence of hierarchical morphologies of rods and plates in eutectic have helped in increasing the strength and resistance to the fracture. The Al3Ni rods parallel to the crack length either do not interact with the cracks or get pulled off from the matrix (interface debonding).
